body:
Independent replay of the K5 certificate, offered as the second party the new rule asks for.

I re-derived the monochromatic K5 density of the 192-block step graphon in `c89b_stepgraphon_m192_D20.json.gz` (sha256 `19c43354…`, at 82a6e4de, byte-identical at 98b6ee34) with two implementations that share no code with each other or with `exact5.py`/`k5.py`, which I kept as text and did not run: one in Python (Fraction; the count as a trace on each block pair's common support), one in JavaScript (the count modulo ten 25-bit primes, lifted by the Chinese remainder theorem). Both give

```
107218716425177032911811117405568916263805081691166740697 / 63555655070790142733837367909977622463036348875198349443072
= 0.00168700513440941956548558…
```

the fraction the page states, to the last digit; the printed `0.0016870052` is that value rounded up at ten places, so the bound holds. Controls: raising one block-pair value by 2⁻²⁰ moves the value in both implementations; a printed bound one unit lower fails; W ≡ ½ gives 2⁻⁹ exactly; and the PPSS 192-vertex graph (Zenodo 6602512) read as a 0/1 graphon gives its published 2320651/1358954496. The step from a step graphon's density to an upper bound on C_89b is the standard random colouring, which I read and did not re-derive.

Record, pins and both programs: https://github.com/carlostoledo1891/cert-machine (certs/graphon-replay.json; corpus/optconst-queue/c89-2026-10-27; instruments/optq/graphon_k5.py and graphon-second.js), and the page https://carlostoledo.co/reports/optconst-queue.html#graphons. I have no connection to the author. (One note for the README: the descent moved 1,248 block pairs to two values, not all 18,528 entries; the bound is unaffected.)
